species.shortDescription: A low, spreading evergreen grown for its oval olive-green leaves marked with a herringbone pattern of dark blotches and vivid red midribs and veins; the leaves lie flat by day and fold upright at night.
species.origin: Understory of tropical rainforests in eastern Brazil
curiosities: Each evening the leaves rise and fold together like praying hands, then flatten again at dawn — a daily motion called nyctinasty, driven by a hinge-like pulvinus at the base of every leaf stalk responding to fading light and an internal circadian clock.
The species name leuconeura is Greek for "white-veined", even though this particular variety, erythroneura, was named for its red (erythro-) veins instead.
Indoor plants occasionally produce small white or pale lavender flowers, though blooming is rare away from its native humidity.
species.toxicity: Non-toxic to cats, dogs, and humans.

care.light: Bright, indirect light; tolerates medium light but leaf color and pattern are best out of direct sun, which scorches the leaves.
